tasks.extracted: UK Biobank, 371,463 people of European genetic ancestry; primary score of 5 variants associated with alcohol use disorder, strongly associated with intake (F statistic 780). Linear Mendelian randomization, odds ratio per 1-SD increase in genetically predicted consumption (an SD not defined in the main text): coronary artery disease 1.38 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.74; P = 6.00×10−3); myocardial infarction 1.37 (1.05 to 1.78; P = 2.00×10−2), above the paper's threshold of P < .008 for six diseases. Weighted median, MR-Egger, MR-PRESSO and analyses excluding abstainers pointed the same way. The disease associations were tested in current drinkers (Table 2 footnote), whose number is not printed.

tasks.locator: Figure 1, hypertension and systolic blood pressure panels (values printed beside the plot); Table 1, intake volume row
tasks.source_read: PMC full text PMC4091648 (saved text and saved figure values)
tasks.extracted: Carriers of the intake-lowering ADH1B variant reported 17.2% fewer UK units a week (one unit 7.9 g of ethanol) than non-carriers. By self-reported drinking, carriers against non-carriers: odds of hypertension 0.95 (0.89 to 1.02) in people reporting no drinking (53,211), 0.98 (0.93 to 1.03) at more than 0 to under 21 units a week (123,870) and 0.89 (0.81 to 0.99) at 21 or more (39,000), test for trend P = 0.197; for systolic blood pressure the trend P was 0.07. The overall hypertension association (0.94) was clear only in the heaviest-drinking stratum.

tasks.extracted: Directional pleiotropy was indicated only for aortic valve stenosis (the main text does not name the test; details in a supplement table), and weighted median and MR-Egger analyses suggested positive associations with it.
